![security-high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/security-high-priority.svg) ![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The static analysis patterns in `BANNED_SOURCE_PATTERNS` do not check for dynamic `import()` calls (e.g., `import('node:http')` or `import('ali-oss')`). An attacker or developer could bypass the offline capability check by using dynamic imports. Add a pattern to detect dynamic imports of banned modules.

```javascript
export const BANNED_SOURCE_PATTERNS = [
  /from\s+['"](?:ali-oss|node-fetch|axios|got|undici|node:http|node:https|http|https)['"]/,
  /require\s*\(\s*['"](?:ali-oss|node-fetch|axios|got|undici|node:http|node:https|http|https)['"]\s*\)/,
  /\bimport\s*\(\s*['"](?:ali-oss|node-fetch|axios|got|undici|node:http|node:https|http|https)['"]/,
  /\bfetch\s*\/,
  /\b(?:cu[r]l|oss[u]til)\b/,
  /process\.env\s*\[?\s*['"]?(?:OSS|ALIYUN|ALIBABA_CLOUD)/,
];
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Import `open` from `node:fs/promises` to support reading only the first few bytes of PDF files in `inspectRows` instead of reading entire files into memory.

```suggestion
import { lstat, mkdir, open, readFile, realpath, stat, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
```

body:
![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `pilot_objects` array has strict constraints `minItems: 3` and `maxItems: 5`. If the pilot size is scaled up or down in the future (e.g., to test a single document or a larger batch of 10 documents), this schema will reject valid preflight receipts. Consider relaxing or removing these constraints to improve extensibility.

```suggestion
    "pilot_objects": { "type": "array", "minItems": 1, "items": { "type": "object", "required": ["document_id", "source_path", "sha256", "size_bytes", "object_key", "validation_result"], "properties": { "document_id": { "type": "string" }, "source_path": { "type": "string" }, "sha256": { "$ref": "#/$defs/sha" }, "size_bytes": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1 }, "object_key": { "type": "string" }, "validation_result": { "enum": ["PASS", "FAIL"] } }, "additionalProperties": false } },
```

Fixed in 06ea9ebc0. Rows are now required to be plain objects before any field, ordering, duplicate, hash, or document-id processing. null/string/number/array rows produce `invalid_row_type`, are excluded from valid rows, and have dedicated negative tests.

Fixed in 06ea9ebc0. `validateInventory` now rejects null, arrays, and primitive roots with `invalid_inventory_root`; missing/non-array `rows` yields `rows_not_array` and an empty fail-closed processing set. Tests cover null/string/number/boolean roots and missing/null/object rows.

Fixed in 06ea9ebc0. The static guard now detects static, dynamic, and require imports for ali-oss, node-fetch, axios, got, undici, node:http/node:https, http/https, node:net, node:tls, and node:dns, plus fetch, curl/ossutil, and provider credential env reads. Every path has a negative test.

Fixed in 06ea9ebc0. Authority inspection now emits typed missing_file, permission_denied, broken_symlink, lstat_failure, stat_failure, symlink_realpath_failure, header_read_failure, and header_close_failure details. Unexpected diagnostics set `authority_audit_status=FAIL_CLOSED`; all four current candidate surfaces inspect PASS.

Fixed in 06ea9ebc0. Authority inspection uses `open()` and reads exactly five bytes for `%PDF-`; a file-ops spy test asserts the requested read length is 5. Full-file reads remain only in the validator where exact SHA-256 verification requires them.

Addressed with a deliberately different fail-closed design in 06ea9ebc0. I did not adopt an all-zero SHA fallback because it would fabricate provenance. Git absence, invalid SHA, missing frozen commit, or mismatch now raises a typed `ProvenanceError`; tests prove Git failure cannot become a zero SHA.

Addressed with a deliberately different fail-closed design in 06ea9ebc0. The generator verifies a frozen source snapshot plus exact input/generator/validator SHA-256 values and fails with typed provenance errors. It never substitutes 40 zeroes. Ambient origin/main is excluded from deterministic generated content.

body: Not adopted by design. This receipt schema is intentionally scoped to the currently authorized 3-5-file pilot contract, so `minItems: 3` and `maxItems: 5` remain. Ajv tests assert both bounds. A future larger/smaller pilot requires a separately reviewed schema version rather than silently widening this gate.

Fixed in 06ea9ebc0. File catches and top-level main catches use `cause?.message ?? String(cause)` semantics, preserve optional OS codes, and return `file_read_error` for non-ENOENT failures. A thrown string fixture confirms stable typed failure without TypeError.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve every candidate path before opening it**

When an intermediate directory is a symlink outside `sourceRoot`, `lstat(absolute)` reports the final target as a normal file, so this branch never calls `realpath` and the validator reads and hashes a file outside the approved root while potentially returning `PASS`. Even for a final-component symlink whose escape is detected, execution continues to `stat`/`readFile`, contradicting the reported zero credential reads; resolve every candidate and stop before reading when its target escapes the approved root.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat recorded integrity failures as audit failures**

When an inspected file is zero-byte, has invalid PDF magic, or is an escaping symlink, `inspectRows` only increments `zero`, `corrupt`, or `escaping`; it does not add an inspection error. Consequently `inspection_status` and `exact_completeness_established` remain successful, and `buildAuthority` can publish `authority_audit_status: PASS`—notably for the ten physical grade-threshold PDFs that the 892-row validator does not inspect.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Canonicalize paths before checking duplicates**

When two rows use aliases such as `data/file.pdf` and `data/./file.pdf` (or `././data/file.pdf`), both resolve to the same file but this normalization leaves them distinct, so the duplicate-source-path check does not fire. With distinct document IDs and the same hash, the content collision is only a warning and the inventory can still pass, defeating the validator's claimed unique normalized-path guarantee.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject unrecognized QP/MS document IDs**

When a QP or MS row uses any otherwise permitted ID that does not match this specialized regex—such as `srcdoc_custom_qp` or the generated `_1` duplicate suffix—the function returns without checking that the ID identifies the source filename. Such a row can pass validation and receive an object key under an unrelated stable ID, so the promised source-to-ID binding is optional precisely for malformed or newly shaped QP/MS IDs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Derive verification matches from the compared values**

A `verified` receipt can provide different values for `expected_sha256` and `downloaded_sha256` (or different expected and remote sizes) while setting `sha256_match` and `size_match` to `true`, and this schema accepts it because the conditional constrains only the booleans and field types. Any consumer treating schema validity as proof of full-byte verification can therefore record corrupted or wrong remote bytes as verified; equality must be checked outside ordinary JSON Schema or represented so the verdict cannot contradict the values.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require remote execution for remote failure evidence**

When `remote_execution` is `false`, this schema still accepts remote-only claims such as `same_key_different_hash`, a non-null observed hash or version, and `partial_upload_possible: true`. Because there is no fixture discriminator or conditional tying these fields to an actual remote attempt, a local-only document can validate as actionable collision or partial-upload evidence and drive recovery decisions based on observations that never occurred.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
